questions.q: What does DORA stand for, and what did the DORA research actually produce?
options: Deployment Orchestration and Release Automation — a CI/CD vendor's internal benchmark
DevOps Research and Assessment — a multi-year research program that identified four metrics correlated with high-performing software organizations
Distributed Operations Reliability Audit — a compliance checklist for cloud providers
DevOps Objectives and Risk Analysis — an internal Google SRE training curriculum
questions.explain: DORA is DevOps Research and Assessment, the research team whose findings were published in Accelerate and the annual State of DevOps report, identifying four metrics that reliably separate high- and low-performing teams.

questions.q: A team merges a change to main at 10:00 AM and it is running in production at 10:45 AM the same day. Which DORA metric does this timestamp difference measure?
options: Change failure rate
Time to restore service
Deployment frequency
Lead time for changes
questions.explain: Lead time for changes is the time between a commit landing on main and that code successfully running in production — exactly the gap described here.

questions.q: Which two of the four DORA metrics are classified as stability metrics rather than throughput metrics?
options: Change failure rate and time to restore service
Deployment frequency and lead time for changes
Deployment frequency and time to restore service
Lead time for changes and change failure rate
questions.explain: Change failure rate (how often a deploy degrades production) and time to restore service (how fast you recover) measure stability; deployment frequency and lead time measure throughput.

questions.q: According to the DORA research described in this lesson, what is the relationship between throughput metrics and stability metrics among elite-performing teams?
options: Elite teams sacrifice stability almost entirely in exchange for high deployment frequency
The two categories are unrelated and DORA found no correlation between any of the four metrics
Elite teams score well on both throughput and stability simultaneously — they are not a trade-off
Elite teams achieve stability by deploying less often than average performers
questions.explain: The DORA research's most notable finding is that throughput and stability move together, not against each other — elite teams deploy constantly, have short lead times, low change failure rates, and fast recovery, all at once.

questions.q: In the lesson's example of pulling DORA numbers out of real systems, where does the change failure rate calculation's numerator come from?
options: A manual quarterly survey asking engineers to rate how confident they felt about each release
The number of deploys that were later tagged as a rollback, hotfix, or an incident caused by that deployment
The number of code review comments left on the pull request before it was merged
The total count of unit tests that passed in the CI pipeline for that build
questions.explain: Change failure rate is failed_deploys / total_deploys, where a deploy counts as "failed" when it required a rollback, a hotfix, or was tagged to a resulting incident — not survey data or test counts.
